q: Where do the ids (9, 8, 10, ...) come from?
o: From the sorted list of different tokens: each token gets its position
why: The same token always gets the same id, and the ids come from the table of known tokens.

q: After 'the', the text had 'sensor' twice and 'cable' once. What comes after 'the'?
why: The toy always picks the most common next token. That is one prediction per loop.

q: What does the generated line start with now?
o: sensor timed ...: the first of a tie wins
why: most_common keeps the first token it counted when two have the same count.

c: print(next_token("battery"))   # 'battery' was never in the text
o: IndexError: the toy has no follower for it
why: The toy only knows what it has seen. Real models cut unknown words into smaller known pieces, so they rarely hit this.

q: What does a longer generation look like?
o: It repeats the same sentence in a loop
It stops at the first full stop
why: Always picking the most common token falls into a loop. Real models sample instead.
